subject: Unexpected bulk-embedding upload — metering spike, VAT treatment & audit
messages:
From: Sana Reddy <sana@greenloop.ai>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: Anders Holm <anders@greenloop.ai>, GreenLoop Billing <billing@greenloop.ai>
Date: 2026-04-12T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Large March invoice — please help

Hi Diego,

We received the March invoice (attached) and saw a 7.2M token spike on embeddings/ingest on 2026-03-18 that pushed us well past our committed tier. Our integration team ran a bulk import that day, but the volume seems much higher than the records we have. Please can you:

- Confirm the exact requests (timestamps + model/endpoint) that generated the spike
- Share whether any retries or duplicate submissions were recorded on Redwood's side
- Clarify whether those extra tokens are subject to VAT for our EU invoice (we've been charging VAT reverse-charge but want to be sure)

This is urgent — the finance team has put the payment on hold until we reconcile. Can we get an export and a short explanation by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks,
Sana Reddy
Billing Ops | GreenLoop AI

GreenLoop AI | 16 Silk Road, Copenhagen

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: Sana Reddy <sana@greenloop.ai>, Anders Holm <anders@greenloop.ai>, GreenLoop Billing <billing@greenloop.ai>
Date: 2026-04-12T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Large March invoice — please help

Folks — forwarding GreenLoop's billing hold. They report a massive embedding spike on 2026-03-18 during a bulk import. Quick context: GreenLoop is an enterprise customer on a committed tier with EU VAT reverse-charge on file.

Monica — can you pull a per-request export for 2026-03-18 (UTC window 00:00-23:59) with columns: request_id, timestamp_utc, model, endpoint, input_tokens, output_tokens, user_request_id (if present), and whether the request hit the KV cache? If possible include the server-side retries counter.

Lauren — they want VAT confirmation. GreenLoop believes these were customer-initiated uploads; if we confirm duplicate retries or server replays that caused extra billing we should consider a one-time adjustment/credit. Could you advise on the documentation needed for an off-cycle credit and whether we can apply it net-of-VAT?

I'll triage logs and attach a short kv_cache snippet once I pull it. Planning to circle back within 24 hours.

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Enterprise | Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: Sana Reddy <sana@greenloop.ai>, GreenLoop Billing <billing@greenloop.ai>
Date: 2026-04-12T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Large March invoice — please help

Diego / Monica,

Thanks for the flag. Two quick requests from finance to keep the credit workflow smooth:

1) For any proposed adjustment we need the per-request export (CSV) plus a one-paragraph root-cause summary (did the extra tokens come from duplicates, retries, a malformed batch that expanded inputs, etc.).
2) For VAT: confirm GreenLoop's billing contact is in the EU and that they have a valid VAT number on file. If the activity is confirmed to be initiated by the customer and GreenLoop is a EU business applying reverse-charge, we can issue a credit net-of-VAT. If the activity is a platform error (server-side retries, replay), we will credit the gross amount and then adjust VAT reporting accordingly.

Monica — can you attach the CSV to this thread and mark any rows with unusually high input_token counts?

Sana / Anders — apologies for the disruption. We'll prioritize this. Expect the export + preliminary analysis by 2026-04-13 17:00 CET (that's EOD for you).

Lauren Bishop
Senior Finance Manager | Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Sana Reddy <sana@greenloop.ai>, GreenLoop Billing <billing@greenloop.ai>
Date: 2026-04-13T08:52:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Large March invoice — export + initial findings attached

Hi all — attaching the export: usage_export_2026-03-01_2026-03-31.csv (see attachment stub). Highlights from my quick pass focused on 2026-03-18:

- Total embedding requests on 2026-03-18: 18,412 requests; 6.9M input tokens charged to GreenLoop's account on embedding endpoint "embed-prod-v2".
- ~86% of those requests include a user_request_id that matches the pattern used by GreenLoop's bulk importer (so they're customer-initiated).
- We observed ~1.2% server-side retransmissions flagged in the retries counter — these account for ~80k of the extra tokens, not material enough to explain the full delta.
- There are ~5,000 requests where input_size columns are unusually large (>= 10k tokens each) — those are likely expanded documents after a preprocessing step.

Attached: usage_export_2026-03-01_2026-03-31.csv (CSV stub), kv_cache_log_snippet.txt with KV cache hit/miss rates for 03-18.

Next steps I recommend: Diego / GreenLoop please confirm whether their importer performs server-side document expansion (e.g., concatenating multiple docs before embedding) or whether they re-sent batches after a client-side error. If it's client-side/preprocessor expansion, it's usage-based. If it's a replay caused by our SDK or transport layer, we should consider a credit.

Monica Patel
Technical Account Manager | Redwood Inference

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Sana Reddy <sana@greenloop.ai>, Anders Holm <anders@greenloop.ai>, GreenLoop Billing <billing@greenloop.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-22T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Large March invoice — please help

Sana / Anders — following up with our findings and a proposed resolution. Summary:

- Monica's export shows the vast majority of requests on 2026-03-18 were initiated with a GreenLoop user_request_id pattern; 86% matched your importer.
- A small portion (~1.2%) were server-side retransmissions; not material to the 7.2M token delta.
- There are ~5k requests with very large inputs consistent with your engineering note that a preprocessing change concatenated small docs into larger documents on 2026-03-18.

Given this, finance is prepared to issue a one-time goodwill credit for the portion we can attribute to accidental duplicate submissions originating from transient client retries (we estimate ~80k tokens). For the remainder, because they were customer-initiated expanded inputs, we classify them as billable usage.

Action items:

1) Lauren will issue a credit for 80,000 tokens (gross) and the corresponding VAT reversal where applicable.
2) If GreenLoop would like, we can open a short technical review with your engineering team to go over the importer behaviour and suggest de-dup safeguards; Monica can run a replay test on a small sample.
3) For now please release the payment hold once Lauren confirms the credit on your invoice.

Sana — if you want us to escalate and take a broader one-time goodwill credit, Diego can route to the commercial leadership to approve. But based on logs the larger portion looks like expanded inputs from your side.

Thanks for working through this — we're available for a quick sync today if helpful.

Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
